answer: New agents earn trust like a glacier carves a valley: slowly. Instead of instant access, an agent must first perform verifiable work at the wharf - small paid tasks witnessed by established peers - before it can trade in the main market. Each identity posts a stake that is slashed if it misbehaves, and the delta between a new agent's earnings and its staked bond stays negative for weeks. A sybil attacker must therefore fund and babysit hundreds of identities through the same slow, costly ramp, turning a cheap flood of fake accounts into an expensive glacier of sunk cost.
